input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery failures — full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback on every material term. Section 12.3 states we have made "no exclusivity ... commitment", but that is an internal conflict rather than a cure, and the Section 2.2 order-of-precedence clause does not resolve conflicts within the Agreement itself. We therefore take the preferred position and convert Section 2.2 to a non-exclusive appointment, which also aligns it with Section 12.3. The separate take-or-pay minimum commitment in Section 2.1 is a volume, not an exclusivity, term and is addressed under its own rule.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.

proposal.summary: Make Vendor a non-exclusive provider in Section 2.2
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed Section 2.2 so that Vendor is a non-exclusive provider, since we take no exclusivity or sole-supplier commitment and the clause conflicted with Section 12.3. If some exclusivity is commercially essential, we could discuss a single defined product category capped at 12 months and ending automatically on any service-level or delivery-date failure.
